title: What scans can and can't tell you

questions.q: A scan flags base64.b64decode on a field called image. What is your next step?
questions.why: Decoding is harmless, and exec on the result isn't. Only the next line can tell.

questions.q: What does a clean scan mean?
questions.why: Run-time names, compiled files and later downloads don't trip patterns.

questions.q: The same pip call is in docs/build.py and at the top of __init__.py. Which is worse?
options: The one in __init__.py, because it runs at every start
The docs one, because it is hidden
They are the same text, so they are equal
questions.answer: The one in __init__.py, because it runs at every start
questions.why: Where a line runs decides what it means.

questions.q: Why might a harmful line have no scary word in it?
options: Opening a path from a web request needs only a missing check
questions.answer: Opening a path from a web request needs only a missing check
questions.why: Plain words can do real damage.

questions.q: What happened in the lab when a new pattern was added?
options: Fewer misses, and the false alarms were still there
questions.answer: Fewer misses, and the false alarms were still there
questions.why: Clean on a bad line fell from 5 to 2, and false alarms stayed at 6.

questions.q: How do you report a hit honestly?
options: Say what the scan found, what you read, and what the line does
Say the pack passed or failed
Give the count of hits as a score
questions.answer: Say what the scan found, what you read, and what the line does
questions.why: A scan points. A reader decides.
